title: Babies Are Born Without Kneecaps
hook: Newborn babies don't have hard kneecaps
summary: A baby's kneecaps are cartilage and start turning into bone around age three. The number of bones actually goes down as you grow.

text: Actually, there's no hard bone in there yet.
Babies are born with kneecaps made of soft cartilage.
Cartilage barely shows up on X-rays,
so the spot where the kneecap goes looks empty.
Cartilage is the soft but tough tissue
that makes up your ears and the tip of your nose.
Around age three, bone starts forming inside the cartilage.
Over several years, it turns into hard bone.

panels.mean: number of bones in a newborn and in an adult

text: As it grows, several of them fuse into one,
so an adult ends up with about 206.

panels.text: You get fewer bones as you grow up?
